body:
The S&P 500 slipped on Tuesday, weighed down by losses in technology stocks and higher oil prices, as traders reacted to a hotter-than-expected annual consumer price index reading for April.

The broad market index was 0.16% lower, closing at 7,400.96, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.71% to 26,088.20. The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 56.09 points, or 0.11%, and ended at 49,760.56. [...] — CNBC's Anniek Bao and Jeff Cox contributed reporting.

The S&P 500 finished Tuesday's session in the red.

The index closed down 0.16% to 7,400.96. The Nasdaq Composite also fell 0.71% to 26,088.20, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average moved up 56.09 points, or 0.11%, to 49,760.56.

— Sean Conlon

Greenlight Capital president David Einhorn said he missed the market's recent rebound, but remains concerned about lofty valuations. [...] The stock is down more than 2.5% Tuesday morning, after jumping 6.5% on Monday. Last week the stock rose 37.7%. It soared by 53% in April after dropping by 18% in March.

From a tech perspective, the retreat of major technology stocks is a significant driver of current market volatility. This pullback influences tech-heavy indices like the Nasdaq but also cascades into the broader S&P 500. The tech sector often leads market momentum, so declines here disproportionally impact market sentiment and index performance. According to Investopedia’s market news, tech stocks slipping contribute heavily to overall indices’ downward trends.
